How verdict works

Every sampled flow is judged twice — once against the real baseline CNPs/CCNPs, once against baseline+candidate — using Cilium’s own pkg/policy engine (the same .Parse() conversion the real agent uses, not a reimplementation). Flow identities come directly from Hubble’s own resolved Endpoint.Identity, so no separate CiliumIdentity lookup is needed.

Known v1 simplifications

Documented in code, not silent:

Simplification What it means
Ingress only Only ingress-at-destination is evaluated — not full bidirectional ingress+egress correctness.
L7/FQDN flows Counted as not simulated rather than guessed — those verdicts live in Envoy/the DNS proxy, not the policy map this engine computes.
Reply packets Skipped (reply (skipped) in the summary) — connection tracking always allows those regardless of CNP ingress rules.
Real identities only Candidate labels with no matching live pod are never exercised by any sampled flow — GuardBee never invents a fake identity.
--last is a ceiling Hubble’s flow buffer is a small recent-flow ring, not persisted history — it may hold fewer flows than requested. Use --follow to accumulate more over time instead of raising --last further.

A 0 newly dropped result can mean “nothing in the sample touched the port you changed,” not “nothing would break” — re-run, raise --last, or use --follow if a result looks too clean.

Two regressions it caught

Both examples are real runs against the author’s own homelab cluster — not synthetic fixtures.

A blank source/destination in the output (e.g. reserved:host) is a non-pod peer, not a bug — most commonly kubelet’s TCP liveness/readiness probe.

Scoped-too-narrow MQTT allow

examples/homeassistant-allow-mosquitto.yaml looks correct — it does correctly keep real MQTT traffic working:

guardbee verdict -n homeassistant \
  examples/homeassistant-allow-mosquitto.yaml

But it would also silently break a Prometheus :8123 scrape and kubelet’s health check on the same port — both confirmed via the Kubernetes API, not guessed. examples/homeassistant-merge-ready.yaml is the corrected version, re-run against the same cluster:

Left: looks correct, isn’t. Right: same candidate, fixed — every real flow unchanged.

Cluster-wide CoreDNS lockdown

The same lesson, one level up. examples/ccnp-coredns-dns-only.yaml is a CiliumClusterwideNetworkPolicy that correctly restricts CoreDNS ingress to DNS queries from any in-cluster pod:

guardbee verdict --all-namespaces --last 15000 \
  examples/ccnp-coredns-dns-only.yaml

It would also break kubelet’s liveness/readiness probes and the observability namespace’s Prometheus scrape, across all CoreDNS pods. examples/ccnp-coredns-merge-ready.yaml adds explicit rules for all three and comes back with zero regressions on the same sample size.

This one needs --all-namespaces, not a single namespace — the regression lives on the source side, which a namespace filter pinned to the destination’s own namespace wouldn’t rule out, and you may not know a CCNP’s full blast radius in advance anyway.
